sentences.text: Hadrosaurus was a large animal that ranged from 7 to 8 meters in length and weighed between 2 and 4 tonnes, with some estimates placing it at 8 meters long, 3 meters tall, and 3 tons in weight.

This dinosaur had a ponderous build, keratinous beaks for cropping foliage, and specialized complex teeth for processing food, featuring a duck-like beak used for pulling leaves from trees and rows of tightly packed, serrated teeth at the back of its toothless, wide beak.

Hadrosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur that used its front legs to support itself while feeding, possessing a row of bony rods along its back supporting its spine and long spines on the underside of its tail to increase surface area.
In 1858, a Hadrosaurus skeleton became the first North American dinosaur known from more than isolated teeth.
In 1868, the Hadrosaurus specimen became the first dinosaur skeleton ever mounted.
Studies using CT scans and fluoroscopy discovered evidence of various tumors, including hemangiomas and metastatic cancer, in Hadrosaurus vertebrae.

The discovery of Hadrosaurus began in 1838 in New Jersey when William Estaugh Hopkins found large bones, and William Parker Foulke saw the bones displayed in Hopkins' home and helped excavate the complete skeleton in 1858.
William Parker Foulke discovered the rest of the Hadrosaurus bones in 1858 after initially finding them in a marl pit, where the animal's body was transported by a river and deposited in the sea.
Hadrosaurus was a herbivore that likely ate leaves and clusters of vegetation, a diet supported by a 1922 stomach content analysis of a hadrosaurid that revealed seeds and twigs.
Hadrosaurus used its powerful jaws to cut and crush tough food with its irregular tooth edges.
It is suggested that Hadrosaurus lived in groups.
The genus Hadrosaurus was named by Joseph Leidy in 1858.
Because the Hadrosaurus skeleton lacks a skull and was viewed as too incomplete, most scientists considered it a dubious name (nomen dubium) for a long time.
A 2011 review by Prieto-Márquez concluded that Hadrosaurus possesses enough characteristics to ensure its validity.
Hadrosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae and is classified within the parent group Brachylophosaurini.
A 2008 study found that Hadrosaurus was more primitive than lambeosaurines and classic hadrosaurines like Edmontosaurus and Saurolophus.
Hadrosaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period, approximately 83.6 to 77.9 million years ago.

Radiometric dating of bivalve shells from the formation where the holotype was found dates the rocks between 80.5 and 78.5 million years ago, placing the animal in the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80.5 to 78.5 million years ago.
Hadrosaurus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
